searchText: It isn't profit if the low-usage users are subsidizing the high usage users. This is a pretty common business strategy, to calculate the "average" operational cost incurred by your users and then kick out any customers who actually fully utilize your service. So you say "X GB/s" under the assumption that 99% of your users won't fully utilize that, and for the 1% who do you just terminate their accounts. in other words, the way to cancel your gym membership is to actually get fit Its probably a shit tier cloud provider, is it one of the 'all you can eat' ones with hidden limits, just like your home broadband connection works? OVH used to be fun (might still be fun) they used to reset your bandwidth caps on a specific day, regardless of when your month of service started, so you could use up your cap twice and then cancel your account. (I don't think they liked people that did that) ~~Hetzner isn't "shit tier", they're basically on the same level as OVH and are of comparable size~~ Oh different convo, my bad I pretty much consider any 'all you can eat' style cloud provider as shit tier, although you are right OVH is not really shit tier if you are not paying for what they sell..... they can't provide what they sell and are shit all the nodes will be in AWS US-East soon anyways if they want the best MEV opportunities
